note: WHOLE SONG, THE SHEET TURNED OVER. LISTEN FOR 2:30–2:50 and 3:18. Read from its other end the eleven-tick cell strikes on 0, 2, 4 and 8 and the four notes rise, F–Ab–C–Eb: the record's own hook, which this tune was written as the falling answer to. The bass already found the notes in that order in the quiet middle. (1) In the side-to-side trade the left guitar plays the tune as written and the right guitar now plays it backwards, five times. Each pair of cells is a palindrome in pitch and spacing; the seam notes repeat across the stereo (low F left then right, Eb right then left). Muted strokes, cajon and kick take the mirrored gaps (1, 1, 3, 2), the bass follows the side with the tune, the mallet still rings only the falling side. The last pair of cells is as written. (2) In the final exchange the melody still shrinks from four cells to two to one, but the last quick one at 3:18 is the rising side, so the slow close answers it falling, home on F. Only left, right, bass, kick and one cajon track changed, only at 2:29.8–2:50.4 and 3:17.9–3:20.2 (checked note for note). The wiw-negative and wiw-return passages are untouched (-73.6 dB residual or lower); each rewritten cell is within 0.15 dB of v9. note: v11, THE HOLE COMES FIRST (section w2, the handover; by subtraction). LISTEN FOR 0:37.5, then 0:45.2, 0:52.9 and 1:00.2. A note passes from the guitars to the ring every third cell, and until now the muted strokes it buys were there at once: the gap was never heard empty. Now, in the cell where a note is given away, the guitars, the bass and the foot let go of its gap, and you hear where it was, the ring sounding across it; the strokes arrive the cell after, where the snare learns that note. The first hole is the handover's own downbeat: crash, ring, and no band until the C (0.42 s). The second, after the C, is 0.62 s; the last two are one stroke each (0.21 s). The cell after the first hole now states the first group in full, as the first cell used to. Removed: 7 bass strokes, 5 from each guitar, 5 from the kick; one guitar and kick stroke moved back in at 0:40; four ring notes held longer. No new part. MEASURED (raw bench): the four gaps fall 13 to 18 dB, and in them the ring stands 2.6 to 8.8 dB over everything else (the crash's tail and the hat); the handover is 0.14 LU quieter. Every other passage, the five card excerpts and the snare-only cell included, moved 0.05 dB or less (the file's loudness trim). SCORE, kept on judgment: 100.0 → 99.256 and 99.829 → 99.136 (seeds 0, 11). All of it is the recurrence term, which secsim had marked ON THE EDGE (share 0.251 against a floor of 0.25): the first heavy span is a little less like its return, likeness 0.64 → 0.60, and one of seven cuts fell under the floor. TRIED AND NOT ADOPTED: (1) the ring striking each note WITH the guitars the cell before it goes: 14 to 17 dB under the chord, not heard. (2) the band resting for the whole cell when the last note goes (0:58–1:00), so the tune is heard alone, then with its negative, then as the negative only: recurrence fell to 88.5 and 77.7 (totals 98.18, 96.30), and it is a second cell without the band before the first, at 1:25, has been heard.
